Authors II/Ernest Hemingway.png.en:
Ernest Hemingway (1899-1961)

Ernest Hemingway was an American novelist and short-story writer born in Oak Park, near Chicago. He began as a journalist and served as a volunteer ambulance driver in Italy during the First World War, where he was wounded. During the 1920s, he lived among American writers and artists in Paris. Experiences of war, travel and journalism recur in his prose, but are reshaped into concentrated stories rather than straightforward autobiography.

Hemingway's restrained style greatly influenced later storytelling. Instead of lengthy explanations, actions, dialogue and what remains unsaid carry the emotions. The Sun Also Rises portrays a disillusioned post-war generation, while A Farewell to Arms combines love with the futility of war. Experiences of the Spanish Civil War lie behind For Whom the Bell Tolls. In The Old Man and the Sea, a fisherman's solitary struggle becomes a story of endurance and defeat. Hemingway received the 1954 Nobel Prize in Literature, with particular reference to this novella and his influence on modern prose style.

Key works:
The Sun Also Rises (1926); A Farewell to Arms (1929); For Whom the Bell Tolls (1940); The Old Man and the Sea (1952).

Authors II/Ernest Hemingway.png.sv:
Ernest Hemingway (1899-1961)

Ernest Hemingway var en amerikansk roman- och novellförfattare, född i Oak Park utanför Chicago. Han började som journalist och tjänstgjorde under första världskriget som frivillig ambulansförare i Italien, där han sårades. Under 1920-talet levde han bland amerikanska författare och konstnärer i Paris. Erfarenheter från krig, resor och journalistik återkom i hans prosa, men omformades till koncentrerade berättelser snarare än raka självbiografier.

Hemingways återhållna stil har haft stort inflytande på senare berättarkonst. I stället för långa förklaringar får handlingar, repliker och det outsagda bära känslorna. Och solen har sin gång skildrar en desillusionerad generation efter kriget, medan Farväl till vapnen förenar kärlek med krigets meningslöshet. Erfarenheter från spanska inbördeskriget ligger bakom Klockan klämtar för dig. I Den gamle och havet blir en fiskares ensamma kamp till en berättelse om uthållighet och nederlag. Hemingway fick Nobelpriset i litteratur 1954, med särskild hänvisning till denna kortroman och hans inflytande på den moderna prosastilen.

Centrala verk:
Och solen har sin gång (1926); Farväl till vapnen (1929); Klockan klämtar för dig (1940); Den gamle och havet (1952).

Authors II/Italo Svevo.png.en:
Italo Svevo (1861-1928)

Italo Svevo was the pen name of Ettore Schmitz, an Italian-language writer from Trieste. The city's meeting of languages and cultures forms part of the background to his writing. He worked for many years in a bank and later in the Veneziani family's marine-paint business. He published his early novels Una vita and Senilità at his own expense, with little success. Business subsequently took up much of his time, but writing never disappeared completely.

His need for English at work brought him into contact with James Joyce, who became both his language teacher and an important source of literary encouragement. Svevo's interest in psychoanalysis provided another impetus for Zeno's Conscience. In that novel, self-explanation becomes uncertain: Zeno tries to understand his troubles and habits, but his account is also full of contradictions and evasions. Irony and psychological observation prevent the reader from taking every explanation at face value. Recognition came late, helped by French critics and Italian writers, among others. Svevo died in 1928 from injuries sustained in a car accident.

Key works:
Una vita / A Life (1892); Senilità / As a Man Grows Older (1898); La coscienza di Zeno / Zeno's Conscience (1923).

Authors II/Italo Svevo.png.sv:
Italo Svevo (1861-1928)

Italo Svevo var pseudonym för Ettore Schmitz, en italienskspråkig författare från Trieste. Stadens möte mellan språk och kulturer hör till bakgrunden för hans författarskap. Han arbetade länge på bank och senare i familjen Venezianis företag för fartygsfärg. De tidiga romanerna Una vita och Senilità gav han ut på egen bekostnad, utan större framgång. Affärslivet tog därefter mycket av hans tid, men skrivandet försvann inte helt.

Behovet av engelska i arbetet förde honom samman med James Joyce, som blev både språklärare och en viktig litterär uppmuntrare. Svevos intresse för psykoanalysen blev en annan impuls till Zenos bekännelser. Där blir självförklaringen osäker: Zeno söker förstå sina besvär och vanor, men hans berättande är också fullt av motsägelser och undanflykter. Ironi och psykologisk iakttagelse gör att läsaren inte kan ta varje förklaring för given. Erkännandet kom sent, med hjälp av bland andra franska kritiker och italienska författare. Svevo dog 1928 av skador efter en bilolycka.

Centrala verk:
Una vita (1892); Senilità (1898); La coscienza di Zeno / Zenos bekännelser (1923).

Authors/August Strindberg.png.en:
August Strindberg (1849-1912)

August Strindberg was a Swedish playwright and prose writer whose work ranged from contemporary satire and autobiographical narratives to radical experiments with theatrical form. The Red Room was his major breakthrough in 1879. Its vivid Stockholm settings and attacks on contemporary institutions helped change the language and subjects of the Swedish novel.

Internationally, he was particularly influential as a playwright. The Father, Miss Julie and Creditors push conflicts over power, gender and marriage to extremes. Later, in works including To Damascus and A Dream Play, he abandoned a strictly realistic stage: time, space and characters could change as they do in dreams. These plays influenced expressionism and later theatre. His autobiographical books are also literary constructions, not neutral records of his life; in The Son of a Servant, for example, a character named Johan carries the narrative.

Key works:
The Red Room; The Son of a Servant; Miss Julie; Inferno; A Dream Play; The Ghost Sonata.

Authors/August Strindberg.png.sv:
August Strindberg (1849-1912)

August Strindberg var en svensk dramatiker och prosaförfattare vars arbete sträckte sig från samtidssatir och självbiografiska berättelser till radikala experiment med teaterns form. Röda rummet blev hans stora genombrott 1879. Med dess levande Stockholmsmiljöer och angrepp på samtidens institutioner bidrog han till att förändra den svenska romanens språk och ämnen.

Internationellt fick han särskild betydelse som dramatiker. Fadren, Fröken Julie och Fordringsägare driver konflikter om makt, kön och äktenskap till sin spets. Senare, i bland annat Till Damaskus och Ett drömspel, övergav han den strikt realistiska scenen: tid, rum och gestalter kunde förändras som i en dröm. Denna dramatik fick betydelse för både expressionismen och senare teater. Strindbergs självbiografiska böcker är samtidigt litterära konstruktioner, inte neutrala protokoll över hans liv; i Tjänstekvinnans son låter han exempelvis en gestalt vid namn Johan bära berättelsen.

Röda rummet; Tjänstekvinnans son; Fröken Julie; Inferno; Ett drömspel; Spöksonaten.

Authors/Dylan Thomas.png.en:
Dylan Thomas (1914-1953)

Dylan Thomas was a Welsh poet and prose writer born in Swansea. His best-known poems include Fern Hill and Do not go gentle into that good night. The Welsh settings of his childhood recur in his work; the farm that gave Fern Hill its name is linked to the poem's memories of childhood and lost innocence. He also wrote the story collection Portrait of the Artist as a Young Dog.

Under Milk Wood is a radio play built from many voices. Over one day in the fictional coastal town of Llareggub, the inhabitants' dreams, desires, memories and daily lives unfold side by side. The lyrical form accommodates both humour and tenderness towards its characters. Thomas worked on the material for a long time and took part in the first stage performances in New York in 1953. The BBC's first British radio broadcast followed in 1954, after his death. The work shows how his writing is an art for the ear, not just for silent reading.

Key works:
Fern Hill; Do not go gentle into that good night; Portrait of the Artist as a Young Dog; Under Milk Wood.

Dylan Thomas (1914-1953)

Dylan Thomas var en walesisk poet och prosaförfattare, född i Swansea. Till hans mest kända dikter hör Fern Hill och Do not go gentle into that good night. Den lyriska formen rymmer både humor och ömhet inför gestalterna. Thomas arbetade länge med materialet och medverkade i de första scenframförandena i New York 1953. BBC:s första brittiska radiosändning kom 1954, efter hans död. Verket visar hur hans författarskap också är en konst för örat, inte bara för den tysta läsningen.

Authors/Franz Kafka.png.en:
Franz Kafka (1883-1924)

Franz Kafka was a German-speaking Jewish writer from Prague. He trained as a lawyer and worked in insurance while regarding writing as his most important task. Only a small part of his work was published during his lifetime, including Die Verwandlung, known in English as The Metamorphosis. Many manuscripts became known only after his death, when his friend Max Brod chose to preserve them despite Kafka's wish that they be destroyed.

Prague was a crucial setting for his life, but Kafka transformed it in his stories rather than simply depicting it. Its offices, courts and buildings become an unfamiliar literary geography. The Franz Kafka Museum emphasises that such places function as metaphors, not addresses that must be identified. Alongside the stories and major novel projects, his diaries and letters offer an entry into his work, relationships and severe self-criticism. His writing is among the twentieth century's most important attempts to create an unsettling form of its own for the human encounter with the outside world.

Key works:
The Metamorphosis; The Judgment; In the Penal Colony; The Trial; Amerika (The Man Who Disappeared).

Authors/Franz Kafka.png.sv:
Franz Kafka (1883-1924)

Franz Kafka var en tyskspråkig judisk författare från Prag. Han utbildade sig till jurist och arbetade inom försäkringsbranschen, samtidigt som han betraktade skrivandet som sin viktigaste uppgift. Under sin livstid publicerade han bara en mindre del av sitt författarskap, däribland Die Verwandlung, på svenska Förvandlingen. Många manuskript blev kända först efter hans död, när vännen Max Brod valde att bevara dem trots Kafkas önskan att de skulle förstöras.

Prag var en avgörande livsmiljö, men Kafka förvandlade den i sina berättelser snarare än att helt enkelt avbilda den. Stadens kontor, domstolar och byggnader blir hos honom en främmande litterär geografi. Franz Kafka-museet framhåller hur sådana platser fungerar som metaforer, inte som adresser som måste identifieras. Vid sidan av berättelserna och de stora romanprojekten ger dagböcker och brev en ingång till hans arbete, relationer och stränga självkritik. Författarskapet hör till 1900-talets viktigaste försök att skapa en egen, oroande form för människans möte med omvärlden.

Centrala verk:
Förvandlingen; Domen; I straffkolonin; Processen; Amerika (Den försvunne).

Fyodor Dostoevsky (1821-1881)

Fyodor Dostoevsky was a Russian novelist, born in Moscow and trained as an engineer in St Petersburg. In 1849, he was sentenced to death following his involvement in the Petrashevsky Circle. The sentence was commuted to hard labour in Siberia, followed by military service. After returning, he wrote the novels that would chiefly establish his international reputation.

In Dostoevsky's writing, ideas are rarely just abstract arguments: they become forces tearing at people. In Crime and Punishment, Raskolnikov's belief that he stands above ordinary moral rules is confronted by guilt and conscience. The Idiot tests compassion and trusting innocence in a harsh social world, while The Brothers Karamazov combines family conflict with a struggle over faith and doubt. The stories' intensity comes from characters who both argue and contradict themselves. His work also includes shorter forms, from the lonely longing of White Nights to the combative narrator of Notes from Underground.

Key works:
White Nights; Notes from Underground; Crime and Punishment; The Idiot; The Brothers Karamazov.

Fjodor Dostojevskij (1821-1881)

Fjodor Dostojevskij var en rysk romanförfattare, född i Moskva och utbildad till ingenjör i Sankt Petersburg. År 1849 dömdes han till döden efter sitt deltagande i Petrasjevskijkretsen. Straffet omvandlades till straffarbete i Sibirien, följt av militärtjänst. Efter återkomsten skrev han de romaner som framför allt kom att ge honom en internationell ställning.

Hos Dostojevskij är idéer sällan enbart abstrakta resonemang: de blir krafter som sliter i människor. I Brott och straff ställs Raskolnikovs föreställning om att stå över vanliga moraliska regler mot skuld och samvete. Idioten prövar medkänsla och godtrogenhet i en hård social värld, medan Bröderna Karamazov förenar familjekonflikt med en kamp om tro och tvivel. Berättelsernas intensitet kommer ur att gestalterna både argumenterar och motsäger sig själva. Författarskapet rymmer också kortare former, från den ensamma längtan i Vita nätter till den stridbare berättaren i Anteckningar från källarhålet.

Centrala verk:
Vita nätter; Anteckningar från källarhålet; Brott och straff; Idioten; Bröderna Karamazov.

Knut Hamsun (1859-1952)

Knut Hamsun was a Norwegian writer who grew up in poverty in Nordland and tried many occupations before his literary breakthrough. Hunger and Pan are among his major early works. The solitary individual, often a wanderer or outsider in conflict with their surroundings, is central to much of this prose. His later writing broadens its perspective towards communities and a strong criticism of modern civilisation.

Growth of the Soil, published in 1917, embodies his idealisation of farming and a life close to the land. He received the 1920 Nobel Prize in Literature for this novel. Hamsun's literary legacy is also tied to his political positions: he supported Nazi Germany and welcomed the German invasion of Norway. His support for Nazism profoundly affected his standing in Norway after the war.

Key works:
Hunger (1890); Pan (1894); Growth of the Soil (1917); Wayfarers (1927).

Authors/Robert Musil.png.en:
Robert Musil (1880-1942)

Robert Musil was an Austrian writer with an unusually broad scientific background. He trained as an engineer and then studied philosophy and experimental psychology in Berlin. His debut novel The Confusions of Young Törless appeared in 1906. He also worked as a theatre critic and essayist, but devoted much of his life to The Man Without Qualities.

The great unfinished novel observes Central European society before the First World War through its protagonist Ulrich. Musil's literary work and scientific interests make him a writer who approaches human beings from several directions, rather than through a single narrative tradition. After the Nazis came to power, he left Berlin for Vienna and later went into exile in Switzerland. He died in Geneva before completing the novel. In 1943, Martha Musil published part of his surviving material, which she also worked to preserve and bring to public attention.

Key works:
The Confusions of Young Törless; Three Women; The Man Without Qualities; Posthumous Papers of a Living Author.

Robert Musil var en österrikisk författare med en ovanligt bred vetenskaplig bakgrund. Han utbildade sig till ingenjör och studerade därefter filosofi och experimentell psykologi i Berlin. Efter nazismens maktövertagande lämnade han Berlin för Wien och hamnade senare i schweizisk exil. Han dog i Genève innan romanprojektet var avslutat. År 1943 gav Martha Musil ut en del av det efterlämnade materialet, som hon också arbetade för att bevara och göra känt.

Stanisław Lem (1921-2006)

Stanisław Lem was a Polish writer who used science fiction to explore questions of knowledge, technology and human limitations. He was born in Lwów, today's Lviv, studied medicine and worked as a mechanic and welder during the German occupation. After the war, he continued his studies in Kraków, but literature and scientific thought came to shape his working life.

In Solaris, encountering an alien intelligence is not a simple adventure of discovery and conquest but a challenge to understanding itself: how can humans comprehend something unlike themselves? Another side of Lem appears in The Cyberiad, where robot constructors and fairy-tale worlds carry satires on power, morality and faith in universal technological solutions. He also wrote essays and speculations about the future. Serious problems of knowledge and comic thought experiments thus belong to the same body of work, rather than two entirely separate sides of it.

Key works:
Solaris; The Cyberiad; The Star Diaries; Summa Technologiae.

Authors/Thomas Mann.png.en:
Thomas Mann (1875-1955)

Thomas Mann was born in Lübeck and became one of the major novelists of German-language literature. His breakthrough novel Buddenbrooks appeared in 1901, and the 1929 Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded primarily for this work. The tension between an orderly bourgeois life and the artist's unconventional feelings and ambitions is a recurring subject, already clear in the story Tonio Kröger.

Mann's writing ranges across short fiction, large-scale novels and essays. His central works include The Magic Mountain and Doctor Faustus alongside Buddenbrooks. His life also took an explicitly political direction: after 1933, he lived in exile, first in Switzerland and later in the United States. During the war, he broadcast radio addresses to German listeners. His long career thus spans both the bourgeois culture of the late German Empire and the European catastrophe that forced him and his family out of Germany.

Key works:
Buddenbrooks (1901); Tonio Kröger (1903); The Magic Mountain (1924); Doctor Faustus (1947).

Modernists/James Joyce.png.en:
James Joyce (1882-1941)

James Joyce was an Irish writer who made Dublin one of the most carefully portrayed cities in modern literature. He left Ireland with Nora Barnacle in 1904 and lived in Trieste, Zurich and Paris, among other places, but kept returning to his home city in his writing. In the stories of Dubliners, everyday life encounters missed opportunities, social constraints and moments of painful insight.

Joyce renewed the novel by letting the movement of thought, associations and language carry the narrative. Ulysses follows Leopold Bloom and Stephen Dedalus through Dublin on a single day, 16 June 1904, while engaging in a dialogue with Homer's Odyssey. A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man explores a young artist's emancipation from family, church and nation. Finnegans Wake became his final major novel project. Together, the books show how a seemingly local world can contain a much larger literary universe.

Key works:
Dubliners (1914); A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man (1916); Ulysses (1922); Finnegans Wake (1939).

James Joyce var en irländsk författare som gjorde Dublin till en av den moderna litteraturens mest omsorgsfullt skildrade städer. Han lämnade Irland med Nora Barnacle 1904 och levde bland annat i Trieste, Zürich och Paris, men fortsatte att återvända till hemstaden i sitt skrivande. I novellerna i Dubliners möter vardagslivet missade möjligheter, sociala begränsningar och ögonblick av smärtsam insikt.

Joyce förnyade romanen genom att låta tankarnas rörelser, associationer och språk bära berättelsen. Ulysses följer Leopold Bloom och Stephen Dedalus genom Dublin under en enda dag, den 16 juni 1904, samtidigt som romanen för en dialog med Homeros Odysséen. A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man skildrar en ung konstnärs frigörelse från familj, kyrka och nation. Finnegans Wake blev hans sista stora romanprojekt. Tillsammans visar böckerna hur en till synes lokal värld kan rymma ett mycket större litterärt universum.

Dubliners (1914); A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man (1916); Ulysses (1922); Finnegans Wake (1939).

Virginia Woolf (1882-1941)

Virginia Woolf was a British novelist, essayist and critic, and a central figure in the Bloomsbury Group. In her prose, memories, sensory impressions and shifting perspectives often matter more than a traditional sequence of events. Mrs Dalloway and To the Lighthouse explore how different people experience a shared reality, and how time changes relationships and family life.

Woolf was also an important feminist thinker. In A Room of One's Own, she examines the conditions facing women writers and the connection between creativity and independence. She founded the Hogarth Press with Leonard Woolf in 1917, giving her a role as a publisher too. Her work encompasses experimental novels, biographies and extensive literary criticism. It combines attention to the fleeting movements of consciousness with questions of gender, culture and who is given space to write.

Key works:
Mrs Dalloway (1925); To the Lighthouse (1927); A Room of One's Own (1929); The Waves (1931).

Virginia Woolf var en brittisk romanförfattare, essäist och kritiker, och en central gestalt i Bloomsburygruppen. I hennes prosa får minnen, sinnesintryck och skiftande perspektiv ofta större betydelse än ett traditionellt händelseförlopp. Mrs Dalloway och To the Lighthouse utforskar hur en gemensam verklighet upplevs olika av olika människor, och hur tiden förändrar relationer och familjeliv.

Woolf var också en betydelsefull feministisk tänkare. I A Room of One's Own undersöker hon kvinnliga författares villkor och sambandet mellan skapande och oberoende. Tillsammans med Leonard Woolf grundade hon Hogarth Press 1917, vilket gav henne en roll också som förläggare. Hennes författarskap omfattar såväl experimentella romaner som biografier och en omfattande litteraturkritik. Det förenar uppmärksamhet på det flyktiga i en människas medvetande med frågor om kön, kultur och vem som får utrymme att skriva.

Centrala verk:
Mrs Dalloway (1925); To the Lighthouse (1927); A Room of One's Own (1929); The Waves (1931).

The Met also notes how Hokusai's landscapes became known for a palette of indigo and imported Prussian blue. Fuji is therefore not merely a background detail but the recurring subject that connects the whole series.

The image is therefore more than a portrait: a small action conveys an entire everyday situation.

The Flirtatious Type, from Ten Types in the Physiognomy of Women

Kitagawa Utamaro (Japanese, c. 1754–1806) | c. 1793

color woodblock print
Dimensions (museum impression): 36.9 x 25.4 cm (14 1/2 x 10 in.)

Utamaro became known for close-up portraits in the genre of bijinga, pictures of beautiful people. This series assigns women different personality traits on the basis of their appearance and encourages comparisons between the figures. The title The Flirtatious Type should therefore be read as part of the series' historical way of categorising women, not as a statement about an identified person's actual character. The museum dates the print to around 1793.
